messages.subject: Re: NAs in setup_date
messages.body_plain:
Dear Gabriella,
the NA basically means you don't know when it was set up / retrieved. In other words, there is no information to base the calculation of trap effort on.  Hence camtrapR insists on not having NAs in these fields.

You have 2 possibilites:
1) In the absence of any other information, you may enter the dates of the first / last image taken at that station (from the record table) into the setup / retrieval columns. That would be a conservative and safe way. Or any other educated guess of a date.
2) remove these cameras

But be aware that the camera operation matrix and subsequently the detection matrix / effort matrix depend on the setup / retrieval dates. For example, if the setup date you enter is too early, you may end up with lots of 0s in the detection matrix and high values in the effort matrix for those days, which may bias computation of detection probabilities.
If you remove stations, you will lose data. So if possible, I'd suggest to go with option 1.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Detection histories with multiple setup and retrieval dates per camera
messages.subject_clean: Detection histories with multiple setup and retrieval dates per camera
messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick,
my apologies I tool to long to get back to you. Only got to look at this now. It seems a little tricky. The sessionCol argument in not implemented in detectionHistory (yet), so for now we need to find another solution.

Here's some ideas:
1) For cameras that basically ran continuously and were only checked on the "retrieval" dates, you could collapse the whole table into one row per camera.

# (assuming only one camera active at any given time at any station, operated continuously, never multiple cameras per station)

# find setup / retrieval by camera
setup_dates     <- as.Date(tapply(stations$Camera.Start.Date, INDEX = stations$Station.Name, FUN = min), origin = "1970-01-01")
retrieval_dates <- as.Date(tapply(stations$Camera.End.Date,   INDEX = stations$Station.Name, FUN = max), origin = "1970-01-01")

# make simplified camera station data frame
stations_simplified <- data.frame(station   = names(setup_dates),
                                  setup     = setup_dates,
                                  retrieval = retrieval_dates)

camop_noproblem2 <- cameraOperation(CTtable = stations_simplified,
                                    stationCol = "station",
                                    setupCol = "setup",
                                    retrievalCol = "retrieval",
                                    writecsv = FALSE,
                                    hasProblems = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d")

camopPlot(camop_noproblem2)

elephant.detection.history2 <- detectionHistory(recordTable           = cameras,
                                                species               = "Loxodonta africana",
                                                camOp                 = camop_noproblem2,
                                                stationCol            = "Station.Name",
                                                speciesCol            = "Genus.Species",
                                                recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                                recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                                occasionLength        = 7,
                                                day1                  = "station",
                                                includeEffort         = TRUE,
                                                scaleEffort       = FALSE)

2) That doesn't seem to be the case in your study however (I see some overlapping deployments, thus multiple cameras running simultaneously at some times). In that case you could try to use the cameraCol argument for the "sessions" and treat the deployments / sessions as different cameras. This is not really true and will result in the retrieval date of one and setup of the other camera on the same day to result in an effort of 2 cameras on that day. So we need a little hack, adding 1 day to the setup days on all but the first session / deployment.

# illustrate the problem when naively using cameraCol
camop_noproblem3_wrong <- cameraOperation(CTtable = stations,
                                    stationCol = "Station.Name",
                                    setupCol = "Camera.Start.Date.modified",
                                    retrievalCol = "Camera.End.Date",
                                    cameraCol = "Session.Number",
                                    byCamera = FALSE,
                                    allCamsOn = FALSE,
                                    camerasIndependent = TRUE,
                                    writecsv = FALSE,
                                    hasProblems = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d")

camop_noproblem3_wrong [,"2018-05-16"]   # date is retieval of one session and setup of next. Thus effort is 2, which is wrong.

# FIX: add 1 day to start day of all deployments except first
stations$Camera.Start.Date.modified <- stations$Camera.Start.Date
stations$Camera.Start.Date.modified[stations$Session.Number != 1] <- stations$Camera.Start.Date[stations$Session.Number != 1] + 1

# calculate camera operation anew
camop_noproblem3 <- cameraOperation(CTtable = stations,
                                    stationCol = "Station.Name",
                                    setupCol = "Camera.Start.Date.modified",
                                    retrievalCol = "Camera.End.Date",
                                    cameraCol = "Session.Number",
                                    byCamera = FALSE,
                                    allCamsOn = FALSE,
                                    camerasIndependent = TRUE,
                                    writecsv = FALSE,
                                    hasProblems = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d")

camop_noproblem3[,"2018-05-16"]   # now its correct

elephant.detection.history3 <- detectionHistory(recordTable           = cameras,
                                               species               = "Loxodonta africana",
                                               camOp                 = camop_noproblem3,
                                               stationCol            = "Station.Name",
                                               speciesCol            = "Genus.Species",
                                               recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                               recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                               occasionLength        = 7,
                                               day1                  = "station",
                                               includeEffort         = TRUE,
                                               scaleEffort      = FALSE)

elephant.detection.history3$effort

But then you need to have a close at the periods when you had multiple cameras operating simultaneously to check that the setup dates are correct and result. cameraCol was intended for stations with multiple cameras (e.g. pairs), so this is not really what it was meant for and the solution is not ideal.

Bottom line: I'd modify the station table and add one day to the setup dates of all deployments when cameras were only checked but ran continuously. Whenever a new camera was deployed or a camera added to an existing station, leave the original date.

Also see the attached workspace.

Please let me know if this helps of if there's new issues.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
if the cameras report it, it would be strange if the data are not recorded in the metadata.
To explore, can you please share the output of
  exifTagNames(..., returnMetadata = TRUE)
?
Thank you!
